stem: A client presents to the emergency department with acute chest pain suspicious for acute coronary syndrome. Which approach to cardiac troponin testing is most appropriate?

options.A: Use serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin measurements interpreted with a validated clinical decision pathway and the clinical picture.
options.B: Rule out myocardial infarction from one early normal conventional troponin drawn immediately after symptom onset.
options.C: Diagnose myocardial infarction from any single detectable troponin value without considering serial change or clinical context.
options.D: Use lactate dehydrogenase instead of troponin because it rises earlier and is more cardiac-specific.

rationale: ACC guidance for acute chest pain centers evaluation on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin used with rapid clinical decision pathways. Serial hs-cTn measurements and change over time are important, especially because very early presentations may precede a detectable rise and elevated troponin can occur from causes other than type 1 myocardial infarction.
educational_objective: Apply serial high-sensitivity troponin testing appropriately in suspected acute coronary syndrome.
source_document_title: 2022 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on the Evaluation and Disposition of Acute Chest Pain in the Emergency Department
source_locator: Key points—hs-cTn with rapid clinical decision pathways; serial hs-cTn measurements are essential; very early presentation can yield false reassurance
source_claim_supported: Serial high-sensitivity troponin interpreted within a validated pathway and clinical context is preferred for acute chest-pain evaluation.
correction_summary: Removed fixed universal rise/peak/day kinetics that vary by assay and rebuilt around current hs-cTn serial-testing guidance.
audit_findings: Correct option reflects contemporary ACC chest-pain pathways.
Single-value and LDH approaches are unsafe/outdated.
Independent second pass found no competing answer.
